pronunciation.title: Say it right from day one

rules.explain: a=AH, e=EH, i=EE, o=OH, u=OO. Always. So CASA is KAH-sah.

examples.t: casa
examples.r: KAH-sah

examples.t: mesa
examples.r: MEH-sah

rules.rule: H is silent, J sounds like H
rules.explain: HOLA is OH-lah (no H sound). J in JUEVES sounds like English H: HWEH-vehs.

examples.t: hola
examples.r: OH-lah

examples.t: jueves
examples.r: HWEH-vehs

rules.explain: Ñ is like NY in canyon: NIÑO = NEEN-yoh. LL and Y sound like Y in yes.

examples.t: niño
examples.r: NEEN-yoh

examples.t: calle
examples.r: KAH-yeh

rules.explain: Tap your tongue once for R. PERRO (dog) rolls longer than PERO (but).

examples.t: pero
examples.r: PEH-roh

examples.t: perro
examples.r: PEH-rroh

rules.explain: Most words stress the middle: HOLA = OH-lah, GRACIAS = GRAH-syahs. An accent mark (á) forces stress there.

examples.t: gracias
examples.r: GRAH-syahs

examples.t: café
examples.r: kah-FEH

alphabet.title: The Vietnamese alphabet (quốc ngữ): 29 base letters
alphabet.explain: Vietnamese writes in Latin with diacritics that mark tone and vowel quality — a letter can wear a hat, a comma, a dot and a hook at the same time. The base alphabet has 29 letters; j and w are essentially unused, and q works only before u.

counting.title: Counting in Vietnamese: 0 to 15
counting.explain: Every number is a syllable with a tone: một, hai, ba, bốn. Eleven and up is mười (ten) + the number: mười một, mười hai, mười ba. Tone matters — the same syllable in a different tone is a different word.
rules: Six tones: flat, rising, falling, creaky (hỏi), question (ngã) and falling-rising (sắc).
d and đ are different: d is English y, đ is the d of door.
c before a/o is k; x before i/e is s.
